intro: If you're searching for an expat tax advisor near you, you're likely dealing with the tax consequences of living or working abroad, or planning a move. You need someone who understands residence, domicile and cross-border tax rules, and you'd prefer to speak with a professional face to face. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK tax adviser who can quote you directly for the work.
need_heading: What people searching for an expat tax advisor usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for an expat tax advisor are navigating a change in their tax situation and want clarity on their UK obligations.
needs: You're leaving the UK and need to understand how the Statutory Residence Test will affect your tax status.
You've already moved abroad and are unsure whether you're still UK resident for tax purposes.
You're receiving UK income such as rental income or pensions while living overseas and need to know how it's taxed.
You're planning to return to the UK and want to organise your affairs before you arrive.
You're worried about being taxed twice on the same income and want to understand how double tax treaties work.
context: Tax advisers who specialise in expat matters can help you apply the Statutory Residence Test, which determines your UK tax residence based on factors like days spent in the UK and where you have ties. They can also explain how double tax treaties between the UK and other countries may prevent you from paying tax twice on the same income. Because 'tax adviser' isn't a protected title, it's worth checking whether the person you speak to holds a qualification such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation (CTA) or the Association of Taxation Technicians (ATT), or is a qualified accountant or solicitor.

Tax advisers who charge a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and HMRC has been tightening standards for paid tax agents. It's reasonable to ask about their qualifications, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you go ahead. iComply does not provide tax advice or regulated services; we simply introduce you to a professional who can help.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Whether you are leaving the UK, already living abroad, or planning to return, and the country involved.
The type of income you have, such as UK rental income, pensions, or overseas earnings.
Any specific concerns you have about residence, domicile, or double taxation.
Whether you have already taken advice or have any deadlines you are working towards.
Your preferred way to speak with the adviser, such as in person, by phone, or online.
Any particular qualification or professional body you would like the adviser to belong to.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the tax adviser
questions: What qualifications do you hold and are you a member of a professional body such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians?
How do you approach the Statutory Residence Test for someone in my situation?
Can you explain how the double tax treaty between the UK and my country of residence might affect me?
What information will you need from me to give advice?
How do you charge for your work and what will the quote cover?
Are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes and do you have professional indemnity insurance?

faqs.q: What does an expat tax adviser do?
faqs.a: An expat tax adviser helps people who live or work abroad, or are planning to, with UK tax matters. They deal with residence, domicile, double tax treaties and UK income while overseas. They can also help you plan before leaving or returning to the UK.

faqs.q: Do I need a specialist expat tax adviser?
faqs.a: If your affairs involve more than one country, a specialist can help you apply the Statutory Residence Test and understand treaty relief. General accountants may not have this expertise. It's worth asking about their experience with expat matters.

faqs.q: How can I check if a tax adviser is qualified?
faqs.a: Tax adviser is not a protected title, so check whether they hold a recognised qualification such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation (CTA) or the Association of Taxation Technicians (ATT), or are a qualified accountant or solicitor. You can also ask about their supervision for anti-money-laundering and professional indemnity insurance.

faqs.q: Will iComply charge me for the introduction?
faqs.a: iComply is a free introduction service for members of the public. We introduce you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly for their work. You only pay the professional for any work they do for you.
